_schema.description: United Kingdom trades-vendor coverage: field service software, lead generation, insurance, payroll and the certification schemes UK trades deal with (Gas Safe Register, NICEIC and OFTEC). Profiles are shorter than the US reviews and focus on UK-specific facts such as gas and electrical certification, HMRC RTI and CIS. Cross-market vendors link to their US reviews where one exists.

vendor_shape.name: string
vendor_shape.category: software | lead-gen | insurance | payroll | agencies | certification
vendor_shape.market_position: string (1-2 sentences on UK market position)
vendor_shape.uk_specific_note: string (what UK contractors need to know: Gas Safe required? CIS deductions? RTI compliance? etc.)
vendor_shape.is_cross_market: boolean (true if also covered in US/other markets)
vendor_shape.cross_market_link: string (URL to existing US review if applicable)

vendors.name: Checkatrade
vendors.tagline: UK trades directory with a free profile, a £30/month Approved plan and lead plans from £59/month
vendors.market_position: Checkatrade is a UK trades directory and lead service run by Vetted Limited in London. Tradespeople can list free, pay £30 a month for the Approved plan with the Checkatrade tick after ID, address and documentation checks, or take a Growth plan from £59 a month that adds a chosen volume of customer enquiries, direct booking and search credit. Checkatrade says memberships are for 12 months and it covers 72 trade industries. In September 2026 Checkatrade Group bought the Rated People brand and website, and jobs posted on Rated People are now matched with Checkatrade members.
vendors.uk_specific_note: You pick the UK postcode areas you work in and, on lead plans, how many leads you want a year. The Checkatrade tick needs ID, address and documentation checks. Since September 2026 Checkatrade members also receive jobs posted on Rated People, whose brand and website Checkatrade Group bought after Rated People Limited went into liquidation.
pros: Free profile to collect and show reviews
Published prices: Approved £30/month, Growth from £59/month
You choose your postcode areas and yearly lead volume
Members also get jobs posted on Rated People since September 2026
cons: Memberships are for 12 months
Only a 'from' price is published for Growth lead plans
The pricing page does not say whether VAT is included
Checkatrade Pay card payments carry fees of 1.29%-1.79%
vendors.typical_pricing: Free £0/month (profile and reviews); Approved £30/month; Growth from £59/month depending on the plan and lead volume. Memberships are for 12 months. The pricing page does not say whether VAT is included

vendors.name: MyBuilder
vendors.tagline: UK marketplace connecting homeowners with tradespeople, owned by Angi Inc. and run within its Instapro Group
vendors.market_position: MyBuilder is a UK online marketplace connecting homeowners with tradespeople, run by MyBuilder Limited in London. Home Advisor Limited has controlled MyBuilder Limited since March 2017, and Angi Inc. lists MyBuilder as its UK marketplace, run within its Instapro Group alongside Travaux.com, My-Hammer, Werkspot and HomeStars. Angi says its international revenue comes mainly from lead fees for consumer matches and membership subscriptions paid by pros.
vendors.uk_specific_note: MyBuilder Limited is registered in England and Wales, with offices in London. MyBuilder's trade pages could not be read for this check, so confirm the current fees and any subscription with MyBuilder before signing up.
pros: Owned by Angi Inc., a US-listed home services company
Separate apps for tradespeople and homeowners
Part of a group running similar marketplaces in six other countries
cons: No prices for tradespeople could be read on MyBuilder's site
Angi says pros on its international marketplaces pay lead fees and membership subscriptions
Confirm vetting and fee terms directly with MyBuilder
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices could be read (mybuilder.com blocked this check). Angi, MyBuilder's owner, says its international marketplaces earn lead fees for consumer matches and membership subscriptions from pros

vendors.name: TrustATrader
vendors.tagline: UK trade directory with a yearly membership fee that says it limits memberships per area and that members never pay for leads
vendors.market_position: TrustATrader is a UK online trade directory. Its trader terms name Trustatrader.com Limited (company no 05489753) with a registered office at 5 Meadway Court, Rutherford Close, Stevenage SG1 2EF, and Companies House lists the company as active, incorporated 23 June 2005. TrustATrader's about page says 'since 2005'. Its home page says memberships are limited per area and, when read on 24 November 2026, showed 458,355 searches made in the last 30 days by visitors.
vendors.uk_specific_note: TrustATrader says all its traders have public liability insurance and provide proof of qualifications and membership of trade associations. Its about page says it verifies that tradesmen have a minimum of two year's experience in their field. Its FAQ lists a minimum of 5 references, a minimum of 2 years experience in your trade and a copy of your insurance documents for applicants. Memberships are limited per area, so a place may not be open for your trade in your area.
pros: TrustATrader says memberships are limited per area so you get a fair share of leads
Its join page lists 'No commission rates' and 'Never pay for your leads'
Its join page lists full use of its branding, including stickers, leaflets and web logos
Its join page says it advertises on national TV and over 60 radio stations nationwide
cons: No membership price is shown on the join page, FAQ or about page; the FAQ says only that it charges a yearly fee
Its terms say you cannot cancel the membership agreement before the end of the 12 month membership period once live on the website
Its terms say the subscription fee is non-refundable; the FAQ mentions a pro-rata refund where a trader is removed after an unresolved complaint and substandard work
Applicants need to provide a minimum of 5 references, 2 years experience in their trade and insurance documents, per its FAQ
Memberships are limited per area, so there may be no place for your trade where you work
vendors.typical_pricing: Membership price not published on the pages read. Its FAQ says it charges a yearly fee; its terms say the fee is payable annually on the anniversary of the start of your subscription, that it does not operate an automatic renewal system, that the 12 month membership cannot be cancelled once live, and that the subscription fee is non-refundable. Its join page lists no commission rates and says you never pay for your leads. Apply by online form or by phone. Pages read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Bark (UK)
vendors.tagline: London-based services marketplace where pros spend credits to respond to customer requests, with up to five pros per request
vendors.market_position: Bark is an online services marketplace founded in the UK by Kai Feller and Andrew Michael, launched in January 2015 and headquartered in London; private equity firm EMK Capital acquired a majority stake in April 2022. The UK site covers business, events, health, home and lessons categories, including plumbing, electrical, roofing and landscaping. Customers post a request and professionals spend credits to respond, and Bark's terms say a maximum of five professionals will contact the customer on a general request.
vendors.uk_specific_note: The UK is Bark's home market: the operator, Bark.com Global Limited, is registered in England and Wales. The UK pricing page explains the credit system but lists no pound prices, and Bark's terms say VAT is payable on top of its fees.
vendors.reputation_flag: Bark's BBB profile shows no BBB accreditation for the company that runs Bark's UK site. The profile, for Bark.com Global Limited under an Austin, Texas address, showed 85 complaints closed in the last three years when checked on 30 September 2026. Under Bark's UK terms you spend credits to respond before you can reach the customer, up to five professionals can contact the same customer, and credits are returned only if you report invalid contact details within 7 days.
pros: No commission on jobs you win, and follow-up messages are free
UK site covering trades and many other service categories
If your first credit pack wins no business, Bark returns the credits once
cons: You spend credits to respond before you know whether the customer will answer
Up to five professionals can contact the same customer
No pound prices on the UK pricing page; VAT is added on top and credits expire after 3 months
Credits returned only for invalid contact details reported within 7 days
vendors.typical_pricing: Pay per response in credits. Bark's UK pricing page says the cost depends on the service, the value of the job and local supply and demand, and lists no pound prices; its terms say VAT is payable on top. No commission; follow-up messages are free. Credits bought on or after 1 November 2025 are valid for 3 months. If your first credit pack wins no business, Bark returns the credits (not cash) once

vendors.name: Hiscox UK
vendors.tagline: Insurer selling public liability, professional indemnity, tool and other business cover to UK tradespeople, online and through its team
vendors.market_position: Hiscox sells business insurance to UK tradespeople and says on its home page it has over 100 years of industry experience. Its terms page names Hiscox Underwriting Ltd (England no. 02372789) and Hiscox Insurance Company Limited (England no. 70234), both at 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ. Its tradesmen page covers public liability, professional indemnity, employers' liability and tool insurance, plus cyber, legal protection, and commercial property, contents and breakdown cover, and says not all types of insurance for tradesman businesses are available for every profession.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Hiscox's terms page says Hiscox Underwriting Ltd is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, and that Hiscox Insurance Company Ltd is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and Prudential Regulation Authority. Its public liability page says employers' liability is not available on its own and must be purchased with public liability, and that it may be legally required if you are an employer. Its tradesmen page says Hiscox does not provide the tailored tool and equipment insurance shown in its builders section, and offers to connect you to its builders' insurance partner. Neither the public liability page nor the tradesmen page mentions Insurance Premium Tax.
pros: Public liability from £5.20 a month, by Hiscox's own figure
Professional indemnity and tool insurance listed on its tradesmen page alongside public liability
Online quotes, or speaking to Hiscox's team on 0800 280 0351, Mon to Fri 9am to 6pm, as its pages state
Terms page states the FCA and PRA authorisation of its UK companies
cons: Employers' liability is not available on its own; it must be purchased with public liability
Hiscox does not provide the tailored tool and equipment insurance in its builders section; it offers to connect builders to a partner
Not all types of insurance are available for every profession, Hiscox says
Only a 'from' price is published, with a footnote that it is based on policies sold; your premium is not shown without a quote
The public liability and tradesmen pages do not mention Insurance Premium Tax
vendors.typical_pricing: Public liability from £5.20 a month. Hiscox's footnote says the figures are based on an average of all public liability policies sold to at least 10% of its customer base between August 2025 and August 2026. The tradesmen page gives no price. Other covers and trades are not priced on the pages read. Neither page mentions Insurance Premium Tax. Pricing page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Simply Business UK
vendors.tagline: Online insurance broker, acquired by Travelers in 2017, offering tradesman cover quotes
vendors.market_position: Simply Business says it started out as a team of five in 2005 and was acquired by its parent company Travelers in 2017. Its Important Information page says Simply Business is a trading name of Xbridge Limited and is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority to act as an insurance intermediary. Its tradesman page shows logos for Allianz, AIG, Axa, Churchill, Covea, Hiscox and Zurich, says it has insurance for over 1,500 trades, says it was chosen by over one million small business and landlord customers, and invites visitors to join over 250,000 tradespeople.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Its public liability page says you can choose from £1 million up to £10 million cover, while its tradesman page also says policies usually offer between £1 million and £5 million; the pages do not explain the difference. The tradesman page says employers' liability is usually required by law if you employ anyone, with a fine of up to £2,500 for every day without cover, and lists tools, business and office equipment, stock, hired-in plant, own plant, contract works, legal expenses and personal accident cover. Its example quote for a self-employed builder shows employers' liability, legal expenses and professional indemnity as not included.
pros: Tradesman page lists ten types of cover, including public liability, tools, contract works, plant, stock, legal expenses and personal accident
Public liability page says you can choose from £1 million up to £10 million cover
Tradesman page shows a real example quote with its price and what is not included
Page metadata for its quote tool describes it as free to compare quotes
cons: Prices depend on a quote: the tradesman page says the cost depends on the types of cover, the risks of your trade, the equipment covered and your location
The example quote page says prices may go up or down from day to day; a footnote says prices are guaranteed for 30 days
The pages give two public liability ranges (£1 million to £10 million, and usually £1 million to £5 million) without explaining the difference
The pages read do not state how Simply Business is paid, such as commission or fees

The Important Information page names insurers (including UK General, Aviva, Finsbury and RSA) that differ from the logos on the tradesman page; the pages read do not say which insurers quote for a given trade
vendors.typical_pricing: Simply Business says the price for tradespeople insurance starts at £5.05 a month, but the cost depends on the types of cover, the risks of your trade, the equipment covered and your location. It shows a real example quote of £7.32 a month (£87.89 a year) for a self-employed builder with public liability of £1,000,000, with employers' liability, legal expenses and professional indemnity not included; the example is dated 8 September 2026 and is based on factors such as employees and location. A footnote says prices are guaranteed for 30 days. Pages read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: AXA Business UK
vendors.tagline: AXA UK's business insurance for tradespeople, with an online quote and a from-price of £7 a month
vendors.market_position: AXA's tradesman page lists four main covers: public liability (£1 million to £10 million, depending on occupation), employers' liability (£10 million as standard), professional indemnity (£100,000 to £5 million) and business contents. Under 'What other cover can I get?' it lists tool insurance, hired-in tools, business equipment, workshops, contract works cover, business interruption and legal expenses. The site's optional extras menu also names hired-in plant, stock, goods in transit and cyber insurance. The page says it is best to get an online quote. AXA says it protects over 867,000 businesses; the footnote for that figure is not shown on the page read.
vendors.uk_specific_note: AXA says it is a legal requirement in the UK to have an employers' liability policy if you have any staff. Its regulatory page names AXA Insurance UK Plc, registered in England and Wales, number 078950, authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, Financial Services Register number 202312, registered address 20 Gracechurch Street, London, EC3V 0BG. The business insurance page says vans are not covered under a business insurance policy and that van insurance must be arranged as its own policy.

AXA says employers' liability is a legal requirement if you have staff, and lists it as £10 million as standard
Other cover listed includes tool insurance, hired-in tools, contract works cover and legal expenses
AXA says it protects over 867,000 businesses

Public liability limits depend on occupation
No prices by trade appear on the page read; the from-price is the only business insurance figure given
The page read does not mention Insurance Premium Tax or how premiums can be paid beyond the 'a month' from-price
The page says vans are not covered under a business insurance policy
vendors.typical_pricing: AXA says customers pay from £7 a month for business insurance; its footnote says 10% of its customers paid this or less between July and September 2026. No other business insurance prices appear on the page. The page does not mention Insurance Premium Tax. Page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Direct Line for Business
vendors.tagline: Direct Line for Business offers tradesperson insurance with a quote online, with covers you choose and optional add-ons
vendors.market_position: Direct Line for Business is a business insurance brand. Its About us page says it was founded in 2007 and that it is part of Aviva. Its home page says it has over 500,000 business policies nationwide. Its tradesperson page lists public liability from £1 million to £10 million and employers' liability up to £10 million, plus tools, stock, own and hired-in plant, contract works and commercial legal expenses cover, with Overnight Tools and Personal Accident listed as add-ons.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Direct Line says its policies are underwritten by U K Insurance Limited (registered in England and Wales No 1179980, registered office The Wharf, Neville Street, Leeds LS1 4AZ), and says U K Insurance Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority, registration number 202810. Its home page says it is proposing to transfer insurance business from U K Insurance Limited to Aviva Insurance Limited, which may affect Direct Line customers, so check which company is named as your insurer. Its tradesperson page says professional indemnity is offered only if you work in an electrical trade.

Tools, stock, own and hired-in plant and contract works are listed as separate covers, each with stated limits and excesses
Its tradesperson page says there are no admin fees to make changes to a policy, and 0% APR if you pay monthly (over 18s, new policies only, subject to eligibility and credit agreement)

Overnight Tools is an optional add-on for an extra premium, with the same limits and excess as the tools cover
The tradesperson page also describes employers' liability as an option you can choose to add, alongside saying it is covered as standard, so confirm what your quote includes
The price-beat offer lists conditions: equivalent cover, proof of the other quote, new policies only, and it is not applicable to van policies or business policies with Home Emergency cover
Direct Line says it is proposing to transfer insurance business from U K Insurance Limited to Aviva Insurance Limited
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no premiums on the pages read. Direct Line says there are no admin fees to change a policy and 0% APR if you pay monthly (over 18s, new policies only, subject to eligibility and credit agreement). Tools cover: you are liable for 10% of each claim, minimum £100, maximum £500. Page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Commusoft
vendors.tagline: Field service and job management software for trades businesses, with digital gas safety certificates and a London headquarters
vendors.market_position: Commusoft is field service software for trades businesses; its UK home page lists Plumbing & Heating, Gas Engineer Software, Electrician Software and Renewable Software among its industries. Its team page says its headquarters are in London, with teams in the US and India, and that since 2006 it has worked with service companies. Its terms name Commusoft Ltd as the provider. Commusoft says it is designed for businesses with 6 or more staff, and its home page shows Trusted by 10,000+ pros and 2.1M+ jobs completed in 2025.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Commusoft's gas engineer page says engineers can complete landlord gas safety certificates (CP12) and other industry forms in the mobile app and send them instantly, that they can work offline with data syncing when the connection returns, and that scheduling can dispatch a gas engineer with the correct qualifications, such as Gas Safe Registered. Its integrations page lists Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Accounting and FreeAgent, plus Wolseley, City Plumbing and Worcester Bosch. The integrations page does not mention Making Tax Digital or CIS. The UK plans page lists no prices and does not mention VAT.

Its gas engineer page says engineers can work offline and data syncs when the connection returns
Integrations page lists Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Accounting and FreeAgent, plus Wolseley, City Plumbing and Worcester Bosch
Its plans page says onboarding is essential, not optional, and is included in the package

Fleet+ and Sales+ are listed as add-ons without prices. The plans page does not mention VAT. Plans page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: BigChange
vendors.tagline: Leeds-based job management and vehicle tracking software for field service businesses, part of Simpro Group
vendors.market_position: BigChange is job management software for UK trade and field service businesses, combining CRM, job scheduling, a mobile app, live vehicle tracking, quotes and invoicing, and business intelligence in one system. It is based in Leeds, says it was founded in 2013, and says it is part of the global Simpro Group, which also includes AroFlo, ClockShark and Simpro. Its contact page gives company number 08189817 and a UK office at Thorpe Park, Leeds. BigChange says it is trusted by 2,200+ field service businesses.
vendors.uk_specific_note: BigChange describes its software as specifically built for UK field service teams and lists 24/7 UK based support. Its integrations page names Xero and Sage, and says an invoice raised in BigChange is automatically pushed into Xero. Its pricing page lists AI dashcams, fleet and fuel cards as extras. The integrations page does not mention Making Tax Digital or CIS.

Vehicle tracking, with AI dashcams, fleet and fuel cards available as extras
Xero and Sage integrations; a REST API is listed as an extra
24/7 UK based support
cons: No published prices; the pricing page offers Request pricing
AI dashcams, fleet and fuel cards are extras listed without prices
Contract length is not stated on the pricing page
No free trial is advertised on the pricing page

All plans include support, CRM, scheduling, mobile app, live tracking, quote and invoice, business intelligence and a collaboration network; AI dashcams, fleet and fuel cards are listed as extras without prices. Pricing page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Joblogic
vendors.tagline: UK field service management software with planned maintenance and gas certificate tools
vendors.market_position: Joblogic is field service management software from Tracer Management Systems Limited (company number 03611671, trading as Joblogic) in Birmingham, with service contracts, SLAs, planned maintenance and digital gas and F-Gas certificates. It says it has run field service work since 1998 and that more than 7,000 UK service businesses now use it.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Joblogic's UK site prices in sterling. Its service delivery page lists digital gas certificates and F-Gas certificates, its field service page mentions F-Gas via REFCOM and 52-week planned maintenance, and its gas engineer page lists tracking of MCS certification and PAS 2035 retrofit assessment records. Its field service page says it syncs to Sage, Xero, QuickBooks, KashFlow or FreeAgent. No payroll features appear on the pages read for this entry. The pricing page does not mention VAT.

Digital gas certificates and F-Gas certificates

Standard has a free trial, no card needed; Premium is priced on request and Enterprise has custom pricing. The pricing page does not say whether VAT is included. Pricing page read 24 November 2026

vendors.name: Powered Now
vendors.tagline: UK job management app for trades, with trade certificates, VAT returns and Making Tax Digital support
vendors.market_position: Powered Now is job management software for UK trades. Its terms name Powered Now Limited, Cypress, Thornley Drive, Teignmouth TQ14 9JH, and Companies House lists POWERED NOW LTD, company number 07647786, as active at the same address. Its home page lists quotes and estimates, invoices with payment links, diary and team scheduling, 80+ trade forms and certificates, and receipt tracking. Its pricing page lists expense tracking, supplier invoices and purchase orders, and Xero and QuickBooks integration. Powered Now says 4,000+ UK trade businesses use it.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Powered Now's pricing page lists prices in sterling plus VAT. vendors.name: Tradify (UK)

vendors.market_position: Sleepless Tradesman is an app for UK trade businesses that, its home page says, writes quotes from photos, sends invoices and answers customer messages, and files receipts from a photo. Its site lists an iPhone app on the App Store, an Android app on Google Play, and a browser version, and offers a free local listing for tradespeople.

vendors.name: BrightPay

vendors.market_position: BrightPay is payroll software from Bright Software Group. Its site footer names Thesaurus Software Ltd trading as Bright Software Group, with an address in Leamington Spa, and HMRC's list shows the supplier as Bright Software Group Ltd. BrightPay says it is used to pay 3.5 million employees every month. Bright says BrightPay desktop reached end-of-life at the beginning of the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026), and that to keep running payroll you need an active BrightPay Cloud subscription.
vendors.uk_specific_note: HMRC's page of recognised payroll software lists BrightPay under paid-for payroll software. Auto enrolment tasks, with cloud file links to NEST, The People's Pension and Smart Pension, as Bright states
Annual or monthly pricing plans, and a free trial, as the vendor states
Bright says gross CIS deductions from BrightCIS can be sent into BrightPay

CIS is handled in a separate product, BrightCIS, according to BrightPay's comparison page

vendors.name: Gas Safe Register
vendors.tagline: The legally required register for businesses doing gas work in Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and Guernsey
vendors.market_position: Gas Safe Register is the register of gas businesses approved by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) under the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998, and it replaced CORGI on 1 April 2009. HSE says a gas engineering business must be on the register to legally undertake gas work within the scope of the Regulations. HSE names Capita Gas Registration and Ancillary Services Ltd, part of Capita plc, as the operator.
vendors.uk_specific_note: Regulation 3(3) says no employer may let employees do gas work in scope, and no self-employed person may do it, unless they belong to a class approved by HSE, which is Gas Safe Register. Regulation 3(1) also requires everyone doing gas work to be competent. HSE says the register covers Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and Guernsey. Registration is renewed each year online or by phone and mail, and HSE prosecutes unregistered gas fitters.
pros: Registration is the legal route to doing gas work in scope as a business
Published fees, renewable online
One register across Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and Guernsey
Registered engineers get an ID card, and the public can check the register online
cons: Registration is renewed each year, with a business renewal fee and an engineer fee
Late renewal adds a charge of £137.78 ex VAT
Everyone doing gas work must be competent, which takes training
vendors.typical_pricing: Fees from 1 April 2026, ex VAT (inc VAT): new registration £319.96 (£383.95); annual business renewal online £139.78 (£167.74), or £171.58 (£205.90) by phone and mail; engineer fee £44.40 (£53.28); physical ID card £15.91 (£19.09); late renewal charge £137.78 (£165.34)

NICEIC's About us page says it assesses over 40,000 NICEIC-certified businesses, with a footnote saying the figure was correct as of 31 December 2023.
vendors.uk_specific_note: NICEIC says its Domestic Installer scheme helps electrical installers comply quickly and easily with Part P of the Building Regulations, and its schemes page lists the scheme's scope as domestic electrical installations and Part P notifiable installations. For the Domestic Installer scheme its page asks for a Qualified Supervisor with at least 2 years' responsibility for electrical work, certificates of technical qualifications for that person, and a minimum of £2 million public liability insurance in the registered trading name. Its schemes page lists the Approved Contractor scheme as covering commercial and industrial electrical installations and domestic installations excluding Part P. The Domestic Installer page does not state which parts of the UK the scheme covers.

vendors.name: OFTEC
vendors.tagline: Trade association and competent person scheme operator for oil, solid fuel, electrical and renewable heating work
vendors.market_position: OFTEC says it is a trade association for liquid fuel heating equipment manufacturers and training providers, and that it also runs a competent persons scheme for businesses and technicians approved to install and maintain oil, solid fuel, electrical and renewable heating equipment. Its about page describes it as a 'not for profit' trade organisation for the heating and cooking industries in the UK and Republic of Ireland. GOV.UK lists OFTEC as one of six competent person schemes for oil appliances (including liquid biofuels), alongside APHC, BESCA, Blue Flame Certification, Certsure and NAPIT.
vendors.uk_specific_note: OFTEC says that in England, Wales, the Channel Isles and Isle of Man its registered technicians are authorised to self-certify that their installation work complies with the regulations, without submitting a building control notice. Its application page asks for qualifications or other proof of technical competence for each technician, public liability insurance with a minimum of £2million, and an initial evaluation of the business by an OFTEC regional inspector that includes an on-site visit and inspection of work. Its about page lists Microgeneration Certification Scheme (MCS), TrustMark and PAS 2030 registration services, and its price calculator offers England, Scotland, Wales and Isle of Man, Channel Islands, Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland as regions; direct debit is not available when registering in the Republic of Ireland.
